image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and rostrum emerging vertically from blue ocean water. The skin is dark grey/black with distinctive white mottling and barnacle clusters (callosities). The rostrum is arched, and the two blowholes are visible at the top. The rest of the body is submerged.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the characteristic arched rostrum and the paired blowholes at the apex of the head, matching the species description.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water interaction at the boundary of the whale's head appears slightly static and lacks the complex displacement and foam expected from such a massive object breaking the surface. It looks slightly 'painted on' rather than physically interacting.

The very tip of the snout appears slightly softened and lacks the sharp, hard definition of bone/cartilage, blending slightly into the air/background, suggesting minor generation blur or structural softness.
